name: scheduling
deprecation_criterion: Superseded when scheduling moves to a different clock source (e.g. a native plugin cron API) or when the tick interval/route become config-driven and this slice's hardcoding is removed.
spec_change_reason: Per-dispatch invalid_output/crash-safety re-emit (stop duplicate PRs) + surface RECONCILE deduped in tick_end. CHANGE 1 (Bug 2 duplicate-PR root cause): run_tick's agent-state re-emit is now PER-DISPATCH. The invalid_output / crash-safety re-emit previously re-dispatched EVERY pending dispatch of a paused agent-state on the FIRST missing/invalid output — re-running IMPLEMENT dispatches that had already written a valid handoff AND already opened a PR, producing DUPLICATE PRs (observed live: one re-emit re-ran 5 already-validated implementers -> 5 duplicate PRs). A new pure helper _partition_pending_dispatches(checkpoint) reads each pending dispatch's output_path and validates it (ad.validate_output) exactly as resume does, partitioning into satisfied (file exists AND schema-valid -> PRESERVED, file left on disk) vs pending-again. _emit_pause_from_checkpoint gained a preserve_valid flag: on the re-emit paths it re-dispatches ONLY the not-yet-valid dispatches and scopes the stale-output delete to those (a preserved-valid output is never deleted / never re-run); on the FRESH first pause (preserve_valid=False) it emits every dispatch and deletes every stale file, byte-identically to before. The checkpoint's pending.dispatches list stays the intact source of truth (narrowing applied at emit time only), so resume still collect_outputs ALL dispatches once every one is valid. A crash-safety re-emit whose dispatches are ALL already valid now APPLIES the collected slot with NO re-dispatch (routed through the resume-apply path) instead of emitting an empty pause — determinism/idempotency preserved, a fresh tick unchanged. CHANGE 2 (additive observability): tick_end.detail now carries deduped=len(reconcile_result.deduped) (the same-issue duplicate loop PRs RECONCILE closed this tick, from the reconcile_result #64 read product read from ctx when RECONCILE is routed, 0 when absent/empty) and the one-line trace appends deduped=<n> ONLY when >0 (mirroring integrate_errored/auto_merge_enabled). verify-integrate (ReconcileResult.deduped) is consumed UNCHANGED; no merge/reconcile/re-emit behavior change from CHANGE 2. Re-anchored the housekeep spec.md baseline 1372->1403 for the already-committed 0.40.0 spec growth (contract.md kept under its strictly-grew gate). Prior reason: clobber preview/apply UX. clobber.py REPLACES the user-facing --yes flag with an internal --apply flag: the DEFAULT invocation (no flag) is a PREVIEW that deletes NOTHING, and --apply actually deletes. Both modes now emit ONE machine-first structured payload {mode:'preview'|'applied', artifacts:[{name,path,exists,action:'would-remove'|'removed'|'absent'}], preserved:[names], loop_intent_present:<bool>} (replacing the old {removed,preserved} shape) so the SKILL can render a WOULD-DELETE/DELETED + PRESERVED table; delete-list computation, deletion, and the payload all stay in the script (spec-rules §1/§4). config/route/adapter-map (+ *.bak/*.migrated) remain NEVER-deleted; idempotent (missing artifact = action 'absent'); never creates the runtime dir; loop_intent_present still read BEFORE deletion. ship/skills/clobber/SKILL.md (v0.2.0->0.3.0, edited via skill-creator): DEFAULT = run clobber.py (preview) + render the tables + key /stop-first advice on loop_intent_present + gate on the user typing the verbatim word 'yes' before running clobber.py --apply; --no-dry-run = run clobber.py --apply immediately (no gate); all --yes references removed; dispatches no subagent. Updated test_clobber_e2e.py to the preview/apply surface + payload shape and re-anchored the housekeep spec.md baseline 1345->1372 for the already-committed 0.39.0 spec growth (contract.md kept under its strictly-grew gate). run_tick/lifecycle-dispositions/heartbeat consumed UNCHANGED; the RECONCILE/reject wiring is untouched. Prior reason: Thread issue_filter_apply_labels into the REPORT flush. run_tick's _flush_report now passes sg.issue_filter_apply_labels(gov) through so project-target loop-filed issues carry the configured PULL-visibility labels (mirroring the existing work_own_filings/issue_filter threading); safety-governance and work-intake source are consumed unchanged. The spec bullet + contract for this were committed this cycle in 6b68c74 (docs/spec.md + docs/contract.md at v0.37.0). Reconciled 7 stale scheduling merge-sink test fakes from the retired auto= kwarg to verify-integrate v0.21.0's gh_pr_merge_sink(pr_ref, repo=None, base_branch=None) signature (behaviour-preserving: auto was unused in every fake body). Prior reason: Surface integration_result.auto_merge_enabled in the tick_end event + one-line trace. run_tick derives auto_merge_enabled_count = len(integration_result.get('auto_merge_enabled', [])) beside the existing merged/integrate_skipped/integrate_errored counts, emits it as tick_end.detail['auto_merge_enabled'], and appends an auto_merge_enabled=<n> token to the one-line trace ONLY when >0 (mirroring the integrate_errored-when-positive convention). It is a PENDING success (PRs on which INTEGRATE enabled GitHub native auto-merge this tick), DISTINCT from integrate_errored. Purely additive: all existing tick_end counts/fields + trace tokens are unchanged; a route with no INTEGRATE (or an older integration_result lacking the key) yields 0 via the .get default. verify-integrate is NOT changed here (it already writes the list). Prior reason: status skill relays status.py's FULL rendered human view VERBATIM in a fenced code block (unfold fix). status.py has rendered a multi-line human view since v0.14.0, but ship/skills/status/SKILL.md still carried the stale v0.1.0 wording ('the script ... prints one status line' / 'report the line it prints ... verbatim'), so the model wrote a one-line prose summary and the full formatted report stayed hidden inside Claude Code's folded Bash tool output (a '+N lines' collapse). The SKILL (v0.1.0 -> v0.2.0, edited via skill-creator) now instructs the model to reproduce status.py's FULL rendered view VERBATIM inside a fenced code block in its reply (never a one-line summary), with the rationale that the assistant-message copy is what lets the user read the whole report unfolded. Added e2e tests test_tick_end_identifiers_e2e.py + test_clobber_e2e.py; re-anchored the housekeep doc baseline spec.md 1232->1269 for the pre-committed spec growth. Registering clobber in build_plugin (lib map + _COMMAND_DESCRIPTIONS + count tests) is a SEPARATE packaging-config touch, deliberately NOT done here (cross-feature follow-up). Prior reason: §3.3.3 /tick single tick + /start owns the drain-loop (SKILL-prose only). /auto-maintainer:tick now runs EXACTLY ONE tick (one route pass through any agent-state pause/dispatch/resume) and STOPS at the terminal: a refire final signal is REPORTED (actionable work remains) but the executor does NOT auto-loop into another tick — one /tick = one tick even when the issue pool is not drained. The drain-loop moved to /auto-maintainer:start, which now OWNS it: tick #1 AND each recurring heartbeat, when a completed tick's final signal is refire, fire /auto-maintainer:tick AGAIN immediately, repeating until a non-refire signal (idle/halt/break), so /start drains the backlog promptly; the heartbeat's PROMPT was changed from the single-tick 'Run one auto-maintainer tick now' to the same drain-loop prompt. KEPT gh_pr_files_source + DEFAULT_PR_FILES_SOURCE, _self_deploy_repo_root (own-checkout detector via bp.SELF_DEPLOY_MARKER), the bp import used ONLY for bp.touches_shipped_src + bp.SELF_DEPLOY_MARKER, the terminal _release_needed call, and the release_needed trace token (now standalone) + tick_end event field. Unrelated gh_pr_state_source/pr_state_source (acted-ledger re-entry), REPORT, and refire are untouched. safety-governance (the now-dead self_deploy knob, removed in a follow-up) and packaging-config (KEEP using bp.touches_shipped_src + bp.SELF_DEPLOY_MARKER; bump_version/package_commit_paths removed in a follow-up) are NOT edited. Prior reason: File-referenced dispatch prompt (prompt_path) — deliver each agent-state dispatch's rendered invocation envelope by FILE REFERENCE instead of inline in the --step/--resume stdout JSON, symmetric with the already-file-based subagent OUTPUT, so the executor (orchestrator) never reads or holds the large rendered envelope. The pause previously emitted dispatches[].prompt (ad.render(env)) INLINE in --step stdout; for a large envelope (an IMPLEMENT dispatch with the work-order body + comments) the Bash stdout was truncated, forcing the orchestrator to re-read the whole output to relay the prompt verbatim — pulling the entire envelope into its context. Fix (edits ONLY in run_tick.py + ship/skills/tick/SKILL.md + docs/tests): _pause_result WRITES ad.render(env) to a deterministic ABSOLUTE file under output_dir, named parallel to output_path ('<state>-<di>-<ii>.json' -> '<state>-<di>-<ii>.prompt.md'), sets rec['prompt_path'], and DROPS the inline prompt; the file is written at the PAUSE (where stale OUTPUT files are cleared) and overwritten each emit, so a crash-safety re-emit reproduces the SAME prompt_path with byte-identical content (rendered from the durable checkpoint round-trip, like output_path). The --step/--resume JSON dispatch entries carry prompt_path (a small absolute path) and NOT the multi-KB inline prompt, so stdout stays small (no truncation); subagent_type/description/isolation/output_path/writes/cardinality/item unchanged. The tick executor skill (v0.6.0) dispatches Agent(subagent_type, description, prompt=<a SHORT reference to entry.prompt_path telling the subagent to read its envelope file IN FULL and follow it literally>, isolation?); the orchestrator does NOT open/read prompt_path — the SUBAGENT reads it. Envelope CONTENT is unchanged — only its delivery (file vs inline) changes; agent_dispatch.render and the subagent agent .md files are untouched; the one-step/resume rules, refire loop, and spend metering are unchanged. agent-dispatch / adapter-wiring / verify-integrate / work-intake / safety-governance consumed UNCHANGED. Prior reason: Refire on ANY workable issue in the pool + surface INTEGRATE merge results and the refire decision (two dogfood fixes). (1) REFIRE POOL-BASED: _work_remains is redefined to _work_remains(work_items, triage_memory, backoff_ledger, threshold, now); it computes candidates = _filter_triage_work_items(work_items, triage_memory) (the existing §3.5.3 skip-filter dropping done/deferred-unchanged) and returns True iff any candidate is classify-acceptable (wi.Triage(now).classify=='accepted') AND not blocked-and-unchanged (backoff blocked_count<threshold OR updated_at strictly after deferred_at_updated_at). make_exit is reworked: when tick_outcome=='empty' AND has_acting_agent (gate KEPT so the read-and-idle default still idles) AND _work_remains(...), it rewrites tick_outcome to 'work-remains'. The old committed-work (un-acted/un-handled work_order) gating is REMOVED — the owner's route has no PRIORITIZE so that gate could essentially never fire. make_exit loads triage_memory + backoff from state_path=ctx.read('state_path'); EXIT's manifest stays reads [tick_outcome, work_items, state_path], writes [tick_outcome]. (2) OBSERVABILITY: the tick_end event detail gains merged (count), integrate_skipped (count), integrate_errored (count), merged_refs (list of merged pr_refs) from integration_result, plus refire:true/false; the one-line trace gains a merged=<n> token (and integrate_errored=<n> when >0). All existing detail keys preserved. lifecycle-dispositions, verify-integrate, work-intake, agent-dispatch, route.json, and the packaging release are NOT touched. Prior reason: Immediate-refire when actionable work remains (owner-requested, DESIGN §3.3.3). The loop should run the NEXT tick IMMEDIATELY when actionable work remains, instead of waiting the heartbeat interval. Adds a pure predicate _work_remains(work_items, backoff_ledger, threshold, now) -> True when ANY work_item is BOTH TRIAGE-acceptable (wi.Triage(now).classify(item)[0]=='accepted') AND not blocked-and-unchanged (NOT (backoff[id].blocked_count>=threshold AND item.updated_at NOT strictly after entry.deferred_at_updated_at)); invalid/closed/stale items never count, and a blocked item updated past the pin IS actionable. make_exit now WRAPS lifecycle-dispositions' Exit: when the inner outcome is 'empty' AND the route has an ACTING agent-state (a dispatch entry carrying a truthy effect, threaded onto the runtime dict as has_acting_agent) AND _work_remains over the REMAINING work (this tick's work_items MINUS items already in the durable acted-ledger MINUS items the doer reported `blocked` this tick), it rewrites tick_outcome to 'work-remains' so EXIT emits refire (RUNNING); it overrides ONLY the 'empty' outcome (restart/fault delegated unchanged). EXIT's manifest now reads [tick_outcome, work_items, state_path], writes [tick_outcome], and emits the inner refire/idle/break/halt; work_items is added to the data-readiness initial set. The read-and-idle DEFAULT route + any empty-pool tick still IDLE (back-compat): with no acting agent-state the override never fires. The tick executor skill documents the refire-loop: a 'refire' final signal runs ANOTHER tick immediately, looping until a non-refire signal (idle/halt/break); cron remains the safety net. lifecycle-dispositions, work-intake, durable-state, verify-integrate, agent-dispatch, route.json, and the packaging release are NOT touched. Prior reason: Advisory REVIEW must ALWAYS flow to INTEGRATE (dogfood unmerged-PR root-cause fix). REVIEW became ADVISORY in the loop redesign (it files findings as issues, it is NOT a merge gate) but its AGENT_PORT_TEMPLATES['REVIEW']['signal_rule'] was still 'nonempty_else_empty' (gate-era leftover): a clean PR yields ZERO review_findings -> the rule emits EMPTY -> a route edge REVIEW--EMPTY-->PERSIST SKIPS INTEGRATE, so integration_result stays empty every tick and mergeable PRs are never merged. Fix: set AGENT_PORT_TEMPLATES['REVIEW']['signal_rule'] to 'always_ok' (the rule already exists in agent_dispatch.compute_signal and returns OK), and flip make_review's deterministic no-op _run to emit 'OK' (was 'EMPTY') while still writing review_findings []. So a zero-finding review emits OK and continues to INTEGRATE. REVIEW's declared emits stay [OK, EMPTY] (verify-integrate REVIEW_MANIFEST UNCHANGED) so seeded routes carrying a REVIEW--EMPTY-->PERSIST edge keep passing validate_signals — the EMPTY edge becomes valid-but-dead (no route.json change). migrate_known_port_entries re-derives a stale REVIEW entry from the template, so a healed entry carries signal_rule='always_ok' automatically. verify-integrate, agent-dispatch, route.json, and the packaging release are NOT touched. Prior reason: Stale/incompatible tick-checkpoint discard-and-fresh (third dogfood crash root-cause fix). The adapter-map migration self-heals the live CONFIG, but a durable tick_checkpoint paused at an agent-state under an OLDER wiring bypasses it: its pending.writes names a slot the current (migrated, seeded) wiring no longer registers (e.g. a v0.7.0 checkpoint paused at REVIEW writing the retired review_verdicts slot). run_tick re-emitted the stale dispatch on --step and applied the subagent output to the unregistered slot on --resume -> fc.ContractError crash. Adds a pure predicate _checkpoint_compatible(checkpoint, ctx) (True when empty or pending writes slot in ctx.registered_slots(), False for a retired/renamed slot) and a discard-and-fresh guard at the top of _run_agent_tick: when the checkpoint is present but incompatible, _clear_checkpoint, record the discard on the tick_start event detail (checkpoint_discarded), and force the FRESH path (resume=False semantics) so the tick re-walks from GUARD and re-pauses with the current migrated writes slot. Applies on BOTH --step and --resume; the fresh re-walk relies on the existing acted-ledger/re-entry idempotency so it never double-acts an open PR. Prior reason: Self-healing known-port adapter-map migration (dogfood REVIEW root-cause fix). A stale persisted project-local adapter-map.json known-port agent entry wired under an older template (e.g. a v0.6.0 REVIEW writing the retired review_verdicts slot with an old output_example) broke the redesigned (FT-C/D) loop where REVIEW writes review_findings. adapter_map_config.migrate_known_port_entries(adapter_map) is a PURE dict->dict transform: for each (port, entry) where ad.is_agent_entry(entry) AND port in AGENT_PORT_TEMPLATES it REBUILDS the entry via _build_agent_entry(port, existing dispatch[0].subagent_type), re-deriving writes/cardinality/output_example/inputs/manifest/signal/effect/isolation from the LIVE template while preserving ONLY subagent_type; script strings, custom-port agent entries, and non-agent entries are left unchanged; returns a NEW dict (no input mutation); idempotent. run_tick passes it as the migrate= hook of its single aw.build_loop(...) call (lazily importing adapter_map_config at the call site to avoid the adapter_map_config->run_tick circular import), so a stale entry self-heals on load before resolve+validate every tick.
